before:
Marsh Drainage Board — Pump Attendance Register

The register is kept at the engine house and signed at each visit. Attendants log the hour of arrival, the readings taken, and any silt lifted from the trash screen. Where two stations call within the same hour and only one attendant is on duty, he attends the intake sluice before the washland gauge, and the washland gauge before the outfall meter. Every station is attended before the shift closes, and no visit may be omitted on grounds of distance. Fuel drawn from the bunker is entered in the right-hand column and countersigned by the district foreman at the month's end.

before:

After discussion the committee agreed that tenants may burn woody prunings on their plots between November and February, provided the heap is lit before three in the afternoon. before:
Borough Museum — Ironwork Catalogue, Entry 62

Entry 62 is a wrought gate leaf, some two metres tall, with a scrolled top rail and four surviving dog bars. It came to the museum in 1953 from the demolition of the old brewery yard and has been displayed against the west wall since the gallery reopened. The scrollwork is of the pattern used by the Fentonbridge forge, and the leaf is by that forge, worked in the 1820s. Two bars have been replaced in mild steel, probably in the 1930s. The leaf is stable and requires no treatment beyond an annual wax; loans are not offered while the wall fixings remain original.

before:
Ferry Pier Trust — Notice to Users of the Slipway

Users are reminded that the slipway byelaw governs launching between the outer beacon and the pier head. The byelaw was made in 1968 and has been enforced by the harbour officer ever since. It forbids launching within thirty minutes of a scheduled sailing, requires trailers to be cleared to the upper yard, and permits shore fishing from the north wall only outside those periods. Copies are held at the office and are posted in the waiting shelter. The trust notes that most difficulties last season arose from trailers left on the apron rather than from launching itself, and asks for continued cooperation.

before:
Harbour Office — Berthing Charges Policy

Charges for visiting craft are raised on departure and are payable at the office or by the box at the gate. The sum due for each night alongside is worked out from the vessel's registered length as entered in her papers, and the resulting figure is rounded up to the nearest pound. Craft on the drying moorings are charged at two thirds of the pontoon figure. Concessions apply to members of affiliated clubs on production of a card, and to craft detained by weather beyond three nights. Disputes are referred to the harbour officer, whose decision is issued in writing within ten working days.

before:

Standpipes are issued from the stores window against a signed docket and returned within seven days. Before issue the storeman checks the backflow valve, fits a fresh washer, and confirms the meter reads zero. Meters recovered last quarter showed an average through-flow of 9.4 cubic metres per hire, which the depot uses when estimating unbilled draw-off. Hirers are told to draw only from marked hydrants and to report any hydrant that leaks after closing. Dockets are held in the stores file for two years.
